q: Top-K 类题目在面试中的一个显著特点是？
q_en: What is one distinctive trait of Top-K interview problems?
options: 所有面试官期待完全相同的标准架构
变体很多，面试官常改需求来测试适应力，应跟随引导
它只考数据结构，不涉及系统设计
只要背下 YouTube 的真实架构就能过
why: Top-K 变体非常多，需求上的小改动会大幅改变设计；有的面试官心里有特定解法，此时应顺势调整而不是试图说服对方。
why_en: Top-K has many variants and interviewers often shift requirements to test adaptability, so ask targeted questions and follow their lead rather than arguing them out of a preferred solution.
options_en: Every interviewer expects the exact same standard architecture.
There are many variants, and interviewers often shift requirements to test adaptability, so follow their lead.
It only tests data structures, not system design.
Memorizing YouTube's real architecture is enough to pass.
optionExplanations: 错。不同面试官关注点差异很大，没有统一标准解。
对。顺着面试官的引导调整，比硬守自己的方案更重要。
错。这题同样考数据流、扩展、一致性等系统设计判断。
错。真实架构会变，死记硬背扛不住追问和变体。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: different interviewers focus on very different things, so there is no single standard answer.
Correct: adapting to the interviewer's lead matters more than defending one fixed design.
Wrong: this question tests data flow, scaling, and consistency judgment like any other system design.
Wrong: real architectures change over time, so memorizing one breaks under follow-up questions.
scenario: 面试给的是 YouTube Shorts 观看 Top-K：45 分钟白板，窗口档位和精确度都可能被中途改口。
scenario_en: The prompt is Top-K views on YouTube Shorts, and in a 45-minute session the interviewer may change the window sizes or the exactness requirement midway.

q: 以下哪些属于本设计敲定的核心功能需求？（多选）
q_en: Which items are core functional requirements for this design? (Select all that apply.)
options: 查询全时段（all-time）的 Top-K 视频，上限 1k 条
查询最近 1 小时/1 天/1 月的 tumbling 窗口 Top-K，上限 1k 条
查询任意历史时间段（如 2025 年查 2024 年 6 月）
支持任意起止时间点的查询
why: 核心需求只有全时段与三档 tumbling 窗口的精确 Top-K；任意时间段与任意起止点被明确划为 below the line，所有查询都默认从当下往回看。
why_en: The system serves precise top-K queries for all-time and tumbling one-hour, one-day, and one-month windows capped at a thousand results, with arbitrary ranges explicitly out of scope.
options_en: Query all-time top-K videos, capped at one thousand results.
Query tumbling one-hour, one-day, and one-month top-K windows, capped at one thousand results.
Query an arbitrary historical range, like June 2024 viewed from October 2025.
Support arbitrary start and end timestamps for any query.
optionExplanations: 对。全时段是两条核心读需求之一。
对。三档窗口同样在核心需求范围内。
错。任意历史区间不在两条核心需求之列。
错。任意起止点同样不在核心需求内。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: precise all-time top-K is one of the core requirements.
Correct: precise top-K for the three tumbling windows is also in scope.
Wrong: arbitrary historical ranges were explicitly scoped out as below the line.
Wrong: arbitrary start and end points are also out of scope.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定时间边界切分、互不重叠的窗口，比如整点到整点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tumbling window is a fixed, non-overlapping time bucket aligned to clock boundaries, such as one full hour at a time.

scenario: YouTube Shorts 观看 Top-K：所有查询只允许从当下往回看，单次最多返回 1k 条。
scenario_en: For Top-K views on YouTube Shorts, every query looks backward from now, and one response is capped at a thousand entries.

q: 当前时间是 10:06，「最近 1 小时」在 sliding window 与 tumbling window 下分别指？
q_en: At 10:06, what does the last hour mean under sliding versus tumbling windows?
options: sliding 是 9:00–10:00，tumbling 是 9:06–10:06
sliding 是 9:06–10:06，tumbling 是 9:00–10:00
why: sliding = [T-1h, T]，随查询时刻连续滑动；tumbling = 对齐整点边界的上一个完整小时，即 [Floor(T-1h), Floor(T)]。
why_en: A sliding window covers the exact hour up to the current moment, while a tumbling window is the last full hour aligned to hour boundaries.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    subgraph S["Sliding（现在 10:06）"]
        A["9:06 → 10:06"]
    end
    subgraph T["Tumbling（现在 10:06）"]
        B["9:00 → 10:00"]
    end
options_en: Both are 9:06 to 10:06.
Sliding is 9:00 to 10:00, tumbling is 9:06 to 10:06.
Both are 9:00 to 10:00.
Sliding is 9:06 to 10:06, tumbling is 9:00 to 10:00.
optionExplanations: 错。这是把两者都当成了 sliding 的定义。
错。sliding/tumbling 的定义正好说反了。
错。这是把两者都当成了 tumbling 的定义。
对。sliding 随查询时刻连续滑动，tumbling 对齐整点边界。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: this treats both windows as sliding, which is incorrect.
Wrong: this swaps the definitions of sliding and tumbling.
Wrong: this treats both windows as tumbling, which is incorrect.
Correct: sliding moves continuously with the query time, while tumbling snaps to hour boundaries.
tradeoff: 紧贴查询时刻的直觉窗口 vs 对齐边界、易于预计算的窗口

termDefinitions.meaning: 随查询时刻连续移动的时间窗口，比如永远是过去一小时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sliding window moves continuously with the query time, always covering, say, the last full hour up to now.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对齐固定边界、互不重叠的时间窗口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tumbling window is aligned to fixed clock boundaries and does not overlap with adjacent windows.

scenario: 现在是 10:06，用户请求「最近 1 小时」Top-K；系统按整点边界预聚合，不支持任意起止点。
scenario_en: It is 10:06 and a user asks for the last hour's Top-K; the system pre-aggregates on clock-hour boundaries and does not support arbitrary start and end points.

q: 补全两种流式窗口的语义：
q_en: Fill in the semantics of the two streaming window types:
text: sliding window 的「最近一小时」随{{查询时刻}}连续滑动；tumbling window 则对齐{{整点边界}}，取上一个完整的小时区间。
why: 这是流式系统里两种主要窗口类型：sliding 更贴近直觉但更难实现，tumbling 有固定边界、天然适合预计算。
why_en: Sliding windows move continuously with the query time, while tumbling windows snap to fixed boundaries and are much easier to precompute.

scenario: 需求澄清阶段，面试官没有说明「最近 1 小时」的窗口语义，你要主动提出一种定义把设计推进下去。
scenario_en: During requirements clarification, the interviewer has not defined what last one hour means, so you need to propose a window semantic that lets the design move forward.
q: 更聪明的开场提议是？
q_en: What is the smarter opening proposal?
options: 提议用 tumbling window，并给面试官反对的机会
先实现 sliding window，因为它更精确
两种窗口都实现再让面试官挑
跳过窗口讨论直接画架构
why: 主动提出 tumbling 展示了 foresight（预见了需求歧义），且 tumbling 远比 sliding 好实现，把难啃的 sliding 留到 deep dive 再谈。
why_en: Proposing tumbling windows up front shows foresight about ambiguous requirements and keeps the initial design simple, deferring sliding windows to a deep dive.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品明确要求「从此刻往前推」的实时体验（例如小时榜要求高新鲜度），就必须支持 sliding window，至少对最短的窗口支持。
options_en: Propose tumbling windows and give the interviewer a chance to object.
Implement sliding windows first because they are more precise.
Implement both kinds of windows and let the interviewer pick.
Skip the windowing discussion and go straight to the architecture diagram.
optionExplanations: 对。主动提出并留出反对空间，展示了对需求歧义的预判。
错。sliding 更难实现，一上来就啃硬骨头不划算。
错。同时实现两套窗口浪费面试时间，不该现在做。
错。跳过窗口讨论会让后续设计缺少语义基础。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: proposing it and leaving room to object shows foresight about ambiguous requirements.
Wrong: sliding windows are harder to build, so starting there wastes early interview time.
Wrong: building both windows now wastes limited interview time.
Wrong: skipping the discussion leaves later design steps without a semantic foundation.
tradeoff: 先提议易实现的 tumbling vs 直接啃更精确但更难的 sliding

q: 如果系统必须支持「任意时间段」查询（例如 2025 年 10 月查 2024 年 6 月的 Top-K），对设计的直接影响是？
q_en: If arbitrary time ranges must be supported, what is the direct design impact?
options: 只需要多加一个时间索引
缓存命中率会更高
预计算基本失效
写入吞吐会下降
why: 任意时间段意味着无法预知要聚合哪些区间，预计算基本失效；这很少是面试官想要的，所以明确把它划为 below the line。
why_en: Supporting arbitrary time ranges kills precomputation and forces general time-series queries, which is why it is explicitly scoped out.
options_en: It only requires adding one more time index.
Cache hit rate would go up.
Precomputation would mostly stop working.
Write throughput would drop.
optionExplanations: 错。索引解决不了『任意区间无法预知』这个根本问题。
错。任意区间会打散命中模式，命中率只会更差。
对。任意区间无法预先聚合，只能退回通用时序查询。
错。这条要求影响的是查询形态，不是写入速度。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: an index cannot fix the fact that arbitrary ranges are unpredictable ahead of time.
Wrong: arbitrary ranges scatter the access pattern, so hit rate would fall, not rise.
Correct: since the ranges can't be known ahead of time, precomputation mostly stops working.
Wrong: this requirement changes query shape, not write throughput.
scenario: YouTube Shorts Top-K 已按「窗口固定、只往回看」预聚合；现在要求支持查 2024 年 6 月。
scenario_en: Top-K on YouTube Shorts is pre-aggregated for fixed backward-looking windows, and now we are asked to support querying June 2024.

scenario: Top-K 的结果集理论上可以无限增长，有人问「能不能查前 100 万个视频」。
scenario_en: A Top-K result set can grow without bound in theory, and someone asks whether the system can return the top one million videos.
q: 合理的约束是？
q_en: What is a reasonable cap for Top-K result size?
options: 支持任意大的 K，用分页机制来解决
限制 K ≤ 100，多数场景已经够用
限制 K ≤ 1000，超出的部分交给别的系统
不设上限，靠请求限流机制兜底
why: 对几乎所有 top-K 应用，1k 是合理上限；给可能无限增长的结果集设实际约束是好习惯，全量排序导出属于另一个系统的职责。
why_en: Capping K at one thousand is reasonable because anyone asking for the top million really wants the full dataset from a different system.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品真的需要全量排序导出（离线分析、数据仓库场景），那是批处理系统的事，不该塞进在线 top-K API。
options_en: Support any size of K and lean on a pagination mechanism.
Cap K at one hundred; that covers most real scenarios.
Cap K at one thousand; anything beyond that belongs to a different system.
Impose no cap at all and rely on request rate limiting instead.
optionExplanations: 错。分页不解决结果集无限增长带来的存储与计算问题。
错。100 对很多真实场景（如榜单展示）偏小，不是通用上限。
对。1k 覆盖绝大多数场景，超大导出该交给另一个系统。
错。限流管的是请求频率，管不住单次结果集大小。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: pagination doesn't solve the underlying storage and compute cost of an unbounded result set.
Wrong: one hundred is too small for many real use cases like leaderboards.
Correct: one thousand covers nearly every use case, and full exports belong to a different system.
Wrong: rate limiting controls request frequency, not the size of a single result set.
tradeoff: 给结果集设实际上限 vs 无限增长的通用查询能力

q: YouTube 视频观看 Top-K 系统敲定的非功能需求包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which nonfunctional requirements are locked in for the YouTube views Top-K system?
options: 观看发生到被计入结果最多容忍 1 分钟延迟
结果必须精确，不做近似（先按此设计，近似留到 deep dive）
查询要在几十毫秒内返回
每秒观看量很小，单机即可处理
why: NFR = 1 分钟计入延迟 + 精确结果 + 几十毫秒读延迟 + 海量观看与视频规模（数值先标 TBD 留待估算）。规模恰恰是巨大的，绝非单机能扛。
why_en: The system tolerates at most a one-minute tabulation delay, must be precise, must answer within tens of milliseconds, and must handle massive view and video volumes.
options_en: Tolerate at most a one-minute delay between a view happening and being tabulated.
Results must be precise; no approximation for now (revisit approximation in a deep dive).
Queries must return within tens of milliseconds.
View volume per second is small enough for a single machine.
optionExplanations: 对。这是事件延迟与计入结果之间的宽限期。
对。先按精确设计，近似留到 deep dive 再谈。
对。几十毫秒的读延迟直接排除查询时现算的方案。
错。规模其实巨大（70B views/day），远超单机。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: this is the grace period between an event happening and it counting in results.
Correct: the design starts precise by default and revisits approximation later.
Correct: a tens-of-milliseconds budget rules out on-the-fly aggregation.
Wrong: the actual scale is massive, seventy billion views a day, far beyond one machine.
scenario: YouTube Shorts 观看 Top-K：70B views/day、约 3.6B 视频，读写都要一条可裁决的量化线。
scenario_en: Top-K views on YouTube Shorts runs at seventy billion views a day over roughly three point six billion videos, so both reads and writes need a number we can design against.

q: 为什么要给「观看发生 → 计入 Top-K」设一个 1 分钟的缓冲？
q_en: Why add a one-minute grace period between a view event and its inclusion in Top-K?
options: 分布式系统里事件可能延迟晚到
为了配合缓存过期时间
数据库每分钟才能提交一次事务
用户每分钟才会刷新一次页面
why: 观看是真实时刻发生的事件，但 09:59:55 的事件可能 10:00:55 才到达系统；1 分钟缓冲回答了「等多久」。这个宽限期后来成了缓存与预计算的空间。
why_en: Events arrive late in distributed systems, so a one-minute buffer defines how long we wait before a view must be tabulated, and that grace period later enables caching and precomputation.
options_en: Distributed systems have delay, so events can arrive late.
To line up with the cache expiration time.
The database can only commit a transaction once per minute.
Users only refresh the page once per minute.
optionExplanations: 对。事件在真实时刻发生，但到达系统可能有延迟。
错。缓存 TTL 是后续优化手段，不是这条 NFR 的来由。
错。数据库提交频率不是设计约束的依据。
错。用户刷新行为不影响事件何时被计入。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: the event happens at a real moment but may reach the system with delay.
Wrong: cache TTL is a later optimization, not the reason for this requirement.
Wrong: database commit frequency has nothing to do with this design constraint.
Wrong: how often users refresh doesn't affect when a view gets tabulated.
scenario: 70B views/day 的观看事件经 Kafka 到达，网络抖动下 09:59:55 的事件可能 10:00:55 才落地。
scenario_en: Seventy billion view events a day arrive over Kafka, and with network jitter an event at 09:59:55 may only land at 10:00:55.

q: 「几十毫秒内返回」这条非功能需求对解空间的直接影响是？
q_en: How does a tens-of-milliseconds read target constrain the solution space?
options: 没什么影响，加机器就行
必须放弃时间窗口功能
必须改用近似算法
排除现算方案，转向预计算加缓存读
why: 几十毫秒内不可能对数十亿行现场聚合，这条要求直接把「查询时现算」踢出解空间；给 NFR 配上数字，正是为了帮你做这类裁决。
why_en: A tens-of-milliseconds latency budget eliminates on-the-fly aggregation and forces precomputation with cache-served reads.
options_en: No real impact; just add more machines.
Time window support must be dropped entirely.
The design must switch to approximation algorithms.
It rules out live aggregation, pushing toward precomputation plus cached reads.
optionExplanations: 错。加机器解决不了对数十亿行现场聚合的时间问题。
错。窗口功能仍是核心需求，不能因延迟要求放弃。
错。精确性是另一条独立的 NFR，这条不强制近似。
对。几十毫秒内不可能现场聚合，必须偏向预计算。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: adding machines doesn't fix the time cost of aggregating billions of rows live.
Wrong: window support is a core requirement and cannot be dropped for this reason.
Wrong: precision is a separate requirement; this one doesn't force approximation.
Correct: tens of milliseconds rules out live aggregation and pushes the design toward precomputed, cache-served reads.
tradeoff: 查询时现算 vs 预计算加缓存服务读请求
scenario: YouTube Shorts Top-K 的读 SLA 定在几十毫秒，而一个窗口的明细有数十亿行。
scenario_en: The read SLA for Top-K on YouTube Shorts is tens of milliseconds, while one window holds billions of raw rows.

q: 面试官给出的规模锚点：YouTube Shorts 的日观看量与内容上传速度约是？
q_en: What rough anchors did the interviewer give for YouTube Shorts daily views and upload rate?
options: 每天 7 亿次观看；每天上传 1 小时内容
每天 700 亿次观看；约每秒上传 1 小时的内容
每天 70 亿次观看；每分钟上传 1 小时内容
每天 7000 亿次观看；每秒上传 1 分钟内容
why: 两个锚点：Shorts 70B views/day、每秒约 1 小时内容上传——它们分别推出后面的 700k TPS 写入和 3.6B 视频总量。
why_en: The interviewer anchors the scale at seventy billion views per day and roughly one hour of content uploaded every second.
options_en: 700 million views a day; one hour of content uploaded per day.
70 billion views a day; roughly one hour of content uploaded per second.
7 billion views a day; one hour of content uploaded per minute.
700 billion views a day; one minute of content uploaded per second.
scenario: 面试官在需求澄清阶段抛出两个规模锚点，帮你判断后续写入吞吐和存储会有多大。
scenario_en: During requirements clarification, the interviewer gives two scale anchors so you can estimate later write throughput and storage pressure.
optionExplanations: 错。7 亿/天差了两个量级，按它算写入只有 8k TPS，会让你把存储方案选小。
对。70B views/day ÷ 100k 秒 ≈ 700k TPS 写入；每秒 1 小时上传累计出约 3.6B 视频。
错。70 亿/天仍差一个量级；每分钟 1 小时的上传也推不出十亿级的视频总量。
错。7000 亿/天把写入夸大到 700 万 TPS，会逼你无谓地跳到近似方案。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: seven hundred million a day is two orders of magnitude low, which lands you at eight thousand writes per second and makes you size storage far too small.

Correct: seventy billion views over a hundred thousand seconds is about seven hundred thousand writes per second, and an hour of upload every second accumulates to roughly three point six billion videos.
Wrong: seven billion a day is still an order of magnitude off, and an hour of upload per minute never reaches billions of videos.
Wrong: seven hundred billion a day inflates writes to seven million per second and pushes you into approximation you do not need.

q: YouTube 视频观看 Top-K 问题的核心实体有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which core entities belong in the YouTube views Top-K problem?
options: Video：被观看的视频
View：观看事件
Time Window：查询关联的时间窗口（all-time/小时/天/月）
User：观看者的完整画像
why: 核心实体只有 Video、View、Time Window 三个；接口很简单，不值得多花时间，观看者画像不在范围内。
why_en: The core entities are just the video, the view event, and the time window, so move on quickly because the interface is simple.
options_en: Video: the video being watched.
View: the view event that happened.
Time Window: the time window a query is scoped to, such as all-time, hour, day, or month.
User: the full profile of the viewer.
optionExplanations: 对。视频是被计数的对象，是核心实体。
对。观看事件是驱动计数变化的输入。
对。时间窗口决定一次查询要聚合哪些数据。
错。观看者画像不在本题范围内，不用建模。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: the video is the thing being counted, so it's a core entity.
Correct: the view event is the input that drives counter changes.
Correct: the time window decides which data a query aggregates.
Wrong: full viewer profiles are out of scope and don't need modeling.
scenario: 45 分钟白板画 YouTube Shorts 观看 Top-K，实体表要小到两分钟能讲完。
scenario_en: On a 45-minute whiteboard for Top-K views on YouTube Shorts, the entity list has to be small enough to cover in two minutes.

q: 本系统对外的 API 大致长什么样？
q_en: What should the public read API roughly look like?
options: GET /views/top-k?window={WINDOW}&k={K}
POST /views，让客户端主动上报观看事件
GET /videos/{id}/views，用来查询单个视频的观看数
用 WebSocket 长连接实时推送全量榜单数据
why: 只需一个读接口：按窗口和 K 查询，返回视频 ID 加观看数的数组；写入侧走上游 Kafka 流，不做 view 上报 API。
why_en: The only API is a single GET endpoint taking a window and K and returning a list of video IDs with view counts.
diagram:
graph LR
    Client[Client] --> API[GET /top-k]
    API --> Cache[(Top-K cache)]
    Cache -->|miss| Store[(Aggregate store)]
    Store --> API
    API --> Client
options_en: GET /views/top-k?window={WINDOW}&k={K}.
POST /views so clients can proactively report their own view events.
GET /videos/{id}/views, used to look up a single video's view count.
Keep a WebSocket connection open to push the full leaderboard in real time.
optionExplanations: 对。一个按窗口和 K 取值的读接口就够了。
错。观看事件走 Kafka 消费管道，不需要客户端主动上报。
错。单视频查询不是本题要的『前 K』语义。
错。推送全量榜单和几十毫秒读延迟的需求不匹配。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: one read endpoint keyed by window and K covers the requirement.
Wrong: writes come from an upstream Kafka stream, so no client-facing report API is needed.
Wrong: querying a single video isn't the top-K semantics this problem needs.

scenario: 观看事件由上游 Kafka 流推来，客户端只需按窗口拉榜单，单次最多 1k 条。
scenario_en: View events are pushed in from an upstream Kafka stream, so clients only need to pull a leaderboard per window, capped at a thousand entries.

q: 为什么这个 API 不太需要考虑分页？
q_en: Why does this API usually not need pagination?
options: 因为 HTTP 协议不支持分页
因为结果永远只有 10 条
响应显式限制在 1k 条以内
因为改用了 gRPC
why: 变长结果集通常要考虑分页，但这里上限 1k、客户端又能用 K 控制数量，分页价值不大；在这种显而易见的部分快速带过是 senior 的时间管理信号。
why_en: Pagination matters little because responses are capped at one thousand results and clients already choose how many they want with K.
options_en: Because HTTP does not support pagination.
Because the result always has exactly ten items.
Because the response is capped at one thousand.
Because the API switched to gRPC.
optionExplanations: 错。HTTP 本身完全支持分页，这不是原因。
错。结果条数由 K 决定，不是固定 10 条。
对。上限 1k 又能用 K 控制数量，分页价值有限。
错。协议换成 gRPC 和是否需要分页无关。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: HTTP fully supports pagination, so that's not the reason.
Wrong: the result size is set by K, not a fixed ten items.
Correct: a one-thousand cap plus a client-chosen K makes pagination low value here.
Wrong: switching protocols to gRPC has nothing to do with needing pagination.
scenario: Top-K 读接口的响应被硬限制在 1k 条以内，客户端还能自己传 K 收窄结果。
scenario_en: The Top-K read endpoint is hard-capped at a thousand entries, and the client can pass K to narrow it further.

q: 本题推荐的整体作战计划是？
q_en: What overall interview plan does this problem recommend?
options: 直接给出最终最优架构，一步到位
先搭基础系统，再逐步优化
先花一半时间做容量估算
从近似算法开始设计
why: 从能工作的系统出发去优化，远好于从「最优」系统出发再设法让它能跑；同时要把出现的瓶颈明确指给面试官，避免显得你没看见。
why_en: Start with a working system that meets the functional requirements, earmark bottlenecks aloud, and then optimize them in the deep dives.
options_en: Jump straight to the final optimal architecture in one step.
Build a basic system first, then optimize it step by step.
Spend half the time budget on capacity estimation up front.
Start the design from an approximation algorithm.
optionExplanations: 错。直接给最优方案往往跳过必要的推理过程。
对。从能跑的系统出发再逐步优化，并主动挂账瓶颈。
错。估算只在需要且影响设计时才做，不该占一半时间。
错。近似是后期可选优化，不该作为设计起点。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: jumping to the optimal design often skips the reasoning the interviewer wants to see.
Correct: start from a working system, optimize step by step, and proactively flag bottlenecks.
Wrong: estimation should happen only when it's needed and influences the design, not for half the time.
Wrong: approximation is a later optional optimization, not the starting point.
scenario: 45 分钟白板题 YouTube Shorts Top-K：700k TPS 写入和几十毫秒读延迟的冲突迟早会暴露。
scenario_en: On the 45-minute Top-K problem for YouTube Shorts, the clash between 700k writes per second and a tens-of-milliseconds read budget will surface sooner or later.

scenario: 系统输入是海量观看事件。你可以从零设计「view 上报 API + 网关 + 负载均衡」，也可以假设上游已把观看写入了某个消息流。
scenario_en: The input is a massive stream of view events; you can either design view ingestion from scratch or assume an upstream system already writes views to a message stream.
q: 更好的开场假设是？
q_en: What is the better opening assumption for the input stream?
options: 自建 view 上报 API，从客户端画起
让播放器直接写数据库
用定时任务轮询播放日志文件
假设已有分区好的 Kafka topic
why: YouTube 里必然有别的系统在播放时记录事件，这个假设合理且省掉一堆样板组件；按 videoId 分区的 topic 还给后续分片提供了天然的「缝」。
why_en: Assuming an existing Kafka view-event topic partitioned by video ID is reasonable, skips boilerplate, and that partition key later becomes the natural sharding seam.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确要求端到端设计（含客户端埋点与采集通道），才需要把上报 API、网关这些组件画出来。
options_en: Build a view-reporting API from scratch, starting from the client.
Have the video player write directly to the database.
Poll playback log files on a fixed schedule.
Assume an already-partitioned Kafka topic exists.
optionExplanations: 错。自建上报链路会占用大量画图时间在样板组件上。
错。播放器直连数据库跳过了所有写入保护与解耦。
错。轮询日志文件延迟高，也不符合真实架构习惯。
对。假设已有分区好的 Kafka 流，省样板还留下分片的缝。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: building the reporting path from scratch spends a lot of drawing time on boilerplate.
Wrong: writing directly from the player skips all write protection and decoupling.
Wrong: polling log files adds latency and doesn't match how real pipelines are built.
Correct: assuming an already-partitioned Kafka topic skips boilerplate and leaves a natural seam for sharding.
tradeoff: 假设上游已有 Kafka 流 vs 自建端到端上报链路

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式消息流平台，这里作为观看事件的上游数据源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed streaming platform, used here as the upstream source of view events.

q: 最初「全时段 Top-K」基础版的数据流是？
q_en: What is the first baseline data flow for all-time Top-K?
options: 客户端跳过服务端，直接查询 Kafka topic 拿数据
由 Flink 完成聚合计算后，直接写入缓存服务
每小时跑一次 MapReduce 作业，对全量数据统计
Consumer 从 Kafka 拉事件更新 Postgres 计数
why: 先搭一个能工作的系统：消费者逐条消费事件更新 Postgres 计数，读侧由 top-K 服务用 SQL 查询；单库写入压力这头「房间里的大象」要主动向面试官点破。
why_en: The basic version has a consumer pulling view events from Kafka and incrementing per-video counters in Postgres, with a load-balanced top-K service querying that table.
diagram:
flowchart LR K["Kafka ViewEvent 流
（按 videoId 分区）"] --> C["View Consumer"] C --> P[("Postgres 计数表")] U["客户端"] --> LB["负载均衡"] --> S["Top-K 服务"] S --> P
options_en: The client skips the server and queries the Kafka topic directly for data.
Flink finishes the aggregation, then writes straight into the cache service.
An hourly MapReduce job recomputes statistics over the full dataset.
A consumer pulls from Kafka and updates the Postgres counter.
optionExplanations: 错。客户端不该直接依赖内部消息流。
错。这一版还没引入 Flink，是后面的优化。
错。MapReduce 全量重算延迟太高，不满足几十毫秒 SLA。
对。消费者逐条更新数据库计数，服务端读库返回，是能跑的第一版。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: clients should not depend directly on an internal message stream.
Wrong: Flink isn't introduced until a later optimization step.
Wrong: hourly full recomputation is far too slow for a tens-of-milliseconds SLA.
Correct: a consumer updates counts and a top-K service reads from the database, the first working version.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用关系型数据库，这里承载视频观看计数表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a relational database, used here to hold the video view-count table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式消息流平台，这里是观看事件的上游来源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed streaming platform, the upstream source of view events here.

scenario: 第一版 YouTube Shorts 全时段 Top-K，先不解决 700k TPS，只求端到端能跑通。
scenario_en: For the first cut of all-time Top-K on YouTube Shorts we ignore the 700k writes per second and just get something working end to end.

scenario: 全时段计数存在 Postgres 的 VideoViews(videoId, views) 表里，views 列建了索引，要高效取前 K 个。
scenario_en: All-time counts live in a Postgres VideoViews(videoId, views) table, and the views column is indexed so the service can fetch the top K efficiently.
q: 哪个查询能高效拿到全时段 Top-K？
q_en: Which query efficiently returns all-time Top-K?
options: SELECT "videoId", MAX("views") FROM VideoViews GROUP BY "videoId";
SELECT "videoId", "views" FROM VideoViews ORDER BY "views" DESC LIMIT k;
SELECT * FROM VideoViews WHERE "views" > 1000000;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM VideoViews;
codeSample:
SELECT "videoId", "views"
FROM VideoViews
ORDER BY "views" DESC
LIMIT k;
why: views 索引本质是「按观看数排好序的视频列表」，查询计划直接从索引头部取 K 条，几乎是 O(k) 的操作。
why_en: With an index on the views column the planner reads the top K entries straight off a sorted index, making the query effectively order of K.
whenOtherWins: 一旦查询带时间窗口（SUM + GROUP BY），这个索引就帮不上忙、会退化成扫描——那是后面 deep dive 要解决的问题。
options_en: SELECT videoId, MAX(views) FROM VideoViews GROUP BY videoId;
SELECT videoId, views FROM VideoViews ORDER BY views DESC LIMIT k;
SELECT * FROM VideoViews WHERE views > 1000000;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM VideoViews;
optionExplanations: 错。分组取最大值没用到有序索引，代价远高于必要。
对。views 索引本身有序，直接从头部取 k 条即可。
错。这是范围过滤，返回的不是排好序的前 K。
错。计数查询和取前 K 视频完全是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: grouping to find the max ignores the sorted index and costs more than necessary.
Correct: the views index is already sorted, so the planner just reads the top k off the front.
Wrong: this is a range filter, not a sorted top-K result.
Wrong: a row count is unrelated to returning the top K videos.
tradeoff: 利用有序索引直接取头 K vs 现场分组/过滤计算

q: 给 views 列加索引让读取近似 O(k)，写侧付出的代价是？
q_en: What write-side cost do we pay for indexing the views column?
options: 写入会丢失部分事件
只能单线程写入
写成本升到 O(log n)
没有任何代价
why: 索引换来了廉价的读，但每次观看写入都要更新索引结构，写成本升到 O(log n)——经典的读写权衡，先挂账后面优化。
why_en: The views index makes reads cheap but every write must update it, turning an order-one append into an order-log-n operation.
options_en: Writes lose some events.
Writes can only happen on a single thread.
Write cost rises to an O(log n) index update.
There is no cost at all.
optionExplanations: 错。加索引不会导致事件丢失，这是持久性问题。
错。索引维护和单线程写入没有必然关系。
对。每次写都要同步更新索引结构，成本升到 O(log n)。
错。索引维护显然是有代价的，读写权衡是常态。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: adding an index doesn't cause event loss, that's a durability concern.
Wrong: index maintenance has nothing to do with single-threaded writes.
Correct: every write now synchronously updates the index, so cost rises to O(log n).
Wrong: index maintenance clearly has a cost; read/write tradeoffs are the norm.
scenario: 全时段 Top-K 计数表有数十亿行，读要几十毫秒返回，于是给 views 列建了索引。
scenario_en: The all-time Top-K counter table holds billions of rows and reads must return within tens of milliseconds, so we index the views column.

q: 为了支持时间窗口查询，表结构要怎么改？
q_en: How should the table change to support time-window queries?
options: 加一个按小时截断的时间戳列
每个视频只保留一行并覆盖更新
把原始事件按 JSON 全量存储
为每个窗口建一个数据库实例
why: timestamp 列截断到小时，一个视频跨多个小时就有多行；这让 SQL 能按时间范围聚合，是最朴素的窗口支持方案。
why_en: Add an hour-truncated timestamp column so each viewed video gets one row per hour, letting SQL aggregate over time ranges.
options_en: Add a timestamp column truncated to the hour.
Keep exactly one row per video and overwrite it in place.
Store the raw event as full JSON blobs.
Spin up a separate database instance for every window.
optionExplanations: 对。按小时截断的时间戳让 SQL 能按范围聚合。
错。覆盖更新会丢掉历史小时的分布信息。
错。JSON 全量存储放弃了列式索引带来的查询效率。
错。为每个窗口起一个数据库实例过度且不必要。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: an hour-truncated timestamp lets SQL aggregate by time range.
Wrong: overwriting in place throws away the per-hour history needed for windows.
Wrong: storing full JSON blobs gives up the query efficiency of indexed columns.
Wrong: a separate database instance per window is overkill and unnecessary.
scenario: 全时段 Top-K 已能工作，现在要加「最近 1 小时/1 天/1 月」的 tumbling 窗口查询。
scenario_en: All-time Top-K already works, and now we need last hour, last day, and last month tumbling window queries.

q: 改成「每视频每小时一行」后，写入次数和存储行数分别发生了什么变化？
q_en: After moving to one row per video per hour, what happens to writes and row count?
options: 写入次数翻倍，行数不变
两者都不变
写入次数不变，但行数急剧膨胀
写入次数减少，行数减少
why: 每次观看仍触发一次写，所以写吞吐没变；但同一视频在每个小时都占一行，行数开始爆炸，这个问题要挂账稍后处理。
why_en: Write volume stays the same since each view is still one write, but storing one row per video per hour makes the row count blow up.
options_en: Write count doubles, row count stays the same.
Neither changes.
Write count stays the same, but row count explodes.
Both write count and row count decrease.
optionExplanations: 错。写入次数并没有翻倍，还是每次观看一次。
错。行数其实会因为按小时分行而明显增加。
对。写次数不变，但同一视频跨小时导致行数暴增。
错。改动只会让行数变多，不会让两者都下降。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: write count doesn't double, it's still one write per view.
Wrong: row count actually rises noticeably once rows are split by hour.
Correct: writes stay the same, but rows explode because one video spans many hours.
Wrong: the change only increases rows, it can't decrease both.
scenario: 计数表从「每视频一行」改成「每视频每小时一行」，观看仍以 700k TPS 涌入。
scenario_en: The counter table moves from one row per video to one row per video per hour, while views still stream in at 700k per second.

q: 窗口版查询（按时间范围 SUM 后 GROUP BY 再取前 K）的执行有什么根本问题？
q_en: What fundamental problem does the window query have when it sums and groups by time range?
options: SQL 语法不支持这种查询
结果不精确
无法加 LIMIT 子句
避免不了全窗口扫描求和
why: 即便 timestamp 有索引，SUM + GROUP BY 也必须把窗口段内所有行读出来聚合；处理数十亿行是分钟/小时级操作，和几十毫秒的 SLA 完全冲突。
why_en: The windowed sum-and-group query cannot avoid scanning every row in the range, and scanning billions of rows takes minutes rather than milliseconds.
options_en: SQL doesn't support this kind of query.
The result becomes imprecise.
You cannot add a LIMIT clause.
A full window scan and aggregate is unavoidable.
optionExplanations: 错。SQL 完全支持 SUM + GROUP BY 这类查询。
错。查询本身依然精确，问题出在速度而非结果。
错。LIMIT 子句可以照常加，语法上没有限制。
对。窗口内每一行都要读出来聚合，数十亿行必然很慢。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: SQL fully supports SUM plus GROUP BY queries.
Wrong: the result is still precise, the problem is speed, not accuracy.
Wrong: a LIMIT clause can be added without any syntax restriction.
Correct: every row in the window must be read to aggregate, which is slow at billions of rows.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库读出某个范围内每一行来满足查询，行数越多越慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A scan means the database reads every row in a range to satisfy a query, so it gets slower as row count grows.

scenario: 窗口 Top-K 用 SQL 在数十亿行明细上 SUM + GROUP BY，读 SLA 只有几十毫秒。
scenario_en: The window Top-K query does a SUM and GROUP BY over billions of raw rows, but the read SLA is only tens of milliseconds.

q: 在「查询成本」这个维度上，全时段 Top-K 和窗口 Top-K 的差别是？
q_en: How do all-time Top-K and window Top-K differ on query cost?
options: 两者查询成本都是 O(k)
全时段近似 O(k)，窗口查询要扫描聚合
窗口查询更快，因为要处理的数据更少
两者查询都必须做全表扫描
why: 全时段的计数是「现成的」，索引直接给出排序；窗口的聚合是「现算的」，没有哪个索引存着任意窗口的和。这个不对称是整道题的核心矛盾。
why_en: All-time top-K reads a sorted index in order-of-K time, while windowed top-K must scan and aggregate every row in the range, and that asymmetry drives the whole design.
options_en: Both cost about the same, O(k).
All-time is near O(k) via the index; windowed queries must scan and aggregate.
Windowed queries are faster because there is less data to process.
Both queries always require a full table scan.
optionExplanations: 错。窗口查询无法像全时段那样直接吃索引。
对。全时段计数现成、窗口聚合现算，这是核心矛盾。
错。窗口内数据量通常仍然巨大，不会更快。
错。全时段查询恰恰能避开全表扫描。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: windowed queries can't lean on the index the way all-time counts can.
Correct: all-time counts are ready-made while windowed sums must be computed on the fly, the core tension here.
Wrong: the data inside a window is still typically huge, not faster.
Wrong: all-time queries specifically avoid a full table scan.
tradeoff: 现成计数走索引 vs 窗口聚合必须现场扫描求和
scenario: 同一张计数表上，全时段榜单走 views 索引，窗口榜单要按时间范围现场求和。
scenario_en: On the same counter table, the all-time leaderboard rides the views index while the window leaderboard has to sum over a time range on the fly.

q: 「每个 Top-K 请求都现查一次数据库」为什么是最先要解决的问题？
q_en: Why is querying the database on every Top-K request the first problem to fix?
options: 查询很重，现算会压垮数据库
数据库连接数不够用
SQL 不支持并发查询
Kafka 消费会因此堵塞
why: 读侧总成本 = 读 QPS × 单次窗口聚合代价，两个因子都很大，是最低垂的果实；NFR 的 1 分钟计入延迟允许结果稍旧，缓存与预计算因此可行。
why_en: Total read cost is read QPS times the cost of one window aggregation, and both factors are huge, so this is the lowest-hanging fruit; the one-minute ingestion allowance lets results go slightly stale, which is what makes caching and precomputation legal.
options_en: Queries are heavy, and live computation would crush the database.
The database doesn't have enough connections.
SQL doesn't support concurrent queries.
Kafka consumption would get blocked by this.
optionExplanations: 对。查询昂贵又量大，是最先要处理的瓶颈，且延迟宽限给了缓存空间。
错。连接数不是这里的根本瓶颈。
错。SQL 完全支持并发查询。
错。数据库压力和 Kafka 消费无直接因果关系。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: expensive queries at high volume would crush the database, and the one-minute grace period leaves room to cache.
Wrong: connection count isn't the underlying bottleneck here.
Wrong: SQL fully supports concurrent queries.
Wrong: database load has no direct causal link to Kafka consumption.
scenario: Top-K 读 QPS 很高，每个请求都触发一次跨数十亿行的窗口聚合；NFR 允许结果最多旧 1 分钟。
scenario_en: Top-K read QPS is high and every request triggers a window aggregation over billions of rows, while the NFR tolerates results up to a minute stale.

scenario: Top-K 服务读请求量巨大，NFR 允许结果落后最多 1 分钟，想先用最简单的手段挡住绝大多数读。
scenario_en: The Top-K service has heavy read traffic, and the NFR allows results to be up to one minute stale, so you want the simplest way to absorb most reads.
q: 首选做法是？
q_en: What should be the first read-side optimization?
options: 旁加分布式缓存，按键缓存整个响应
给数据库加一批只读副本
每台服务器用本地文件缓存
把 Postgres 换成写入更快的数据库
why: 命中直接返回、未命中才现算并回填；查询形态固定（窗口 × K），按键缓存整个响应最简单有效。
why_en: Put a distributed cache in front of the top-K service keyed by window and truncated timestamp, storing the whole response with a multi-hour TTL.
whenOtherWins: 只读副本适合「查询形态多样、无法按键缓存」的读扩展场景；这里响应可枚举，按键缓存性价比高得多。
options_en: Add a distributed cache next to the service, caching the whole response by key.
Add a batch of read replicas to the database.
Use a local file cache on each server.
Replace Postgres with a faster-writing database.
optionExplanations: 对。查询形态固定，缓存一整份响应最省事。
错。只读副本适合查询多样、无法按键缓存的场景。
错。本地文件缓存无法在实例间共享，命中率差。
错。换数据库解决不了『每次请求都现算』这个根因。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: the query shape is fixed, so caching the whole response by key is simplest and effective.
Wrong: read replicas fit diverse queries that can't be cached by key, not this case.
Wrong: a local file cache isn't shared across instances, so hit rate suffers.
Wrong: swapping databases doesn't fix the root cause of computing on every request.
tradeoff: 按键缓存整份响应 vs 加只读副本分摊查询

q: 缓存命中时的典型返回时间量级是？
q_en: What is the typical latency order of a cache hit?
options: 几百毫秒
亚毫秒级
几秒
与数据库现算相当
why: 多数分布式缓存亚毫秒返回，命中请求（绝大多数流量）轻松满足 SLA；剩下的麻烦全在未命中路径上。
why_en: Cache hits return in sub-millisecond time, comfortably inside the tens-of-milliseconds requirement, leaving only the miss path as a problem.
options_en: A few hundred milliseconds.
Sub-millisecond.
A few seconds.
About the same as computing live from the database.
scenario: Top-K 榜单已预算好放进分布式缓存，读 SLA 是几十毫秒，绝大多数流量都会命中。
scenario_en: The Top-K leaderboard is precomputed into a distributed cache, the read SLA is tens of milliseconds, and the vast majority of traffic hits the cache.
optionExplanations: 错。几百毫秒是跨区域网络或冷存储的量级，本地分布式缓存不会这么慢。
对。亚毫秒 = 一次内存查表加一跳网络，几十毫秒的读 SLA 因此留有充足余量。
错。秒级是现场聚合数百 GB 的量级，正是缓存要绕开的那条路径。
错。命中若和现算一样慢，缓存就失去意义：它的价值就是把聚合换成一次内存读。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: hundreds of milliseconds is what a cross-region hop or cold storage costs, not a local distributed cache.
Correct: sub-millisecond is one in-memory lookup plus a network hop, so a tens-of-milliseconds read SLA has plenty of headroom.
Wrong: seconds is what aggregating hundreds of gigabytes on the fly costs, which is exactly the path the cache exists to avoid.
Wrong: if a hit were as slow as computing it fresh the cache would be pointless, since its value is turning an aggregation into one memory read.

q: 纯 TTL 缓存方案在缓存过期瞬间会同时出现哪两个问题？
q_en: What two problems appear when a pure TTL cache expires?
options: 内存泄漏和网络分区
缓存永不过期和数据丢失
Kafka 积压和消费者宕机
请求洪水打库，且现算击穿 SLA
why: 过期后所有请求同时未命中：数据库被打爆是其一，更糟的是每个请求都要等慢查询完成——SLA 直接破。前者有缓解手段，后者需要更根本的改造。
why_en: When the cache expires you get a thundering flood on the database and every request also breaks the latency SLA while waiting on the slow recompute.
options_en: Memory leak and network partition.
The cache never expires and data is lost.
Kafka backlog and consumer crashes.
A request flood hits the database, and live computation blows the SLA.
optionExplanations: 错。这两个词和缓存过期问题没有直接关系。
错。TTL 缓存本来就会过期，不存在『永不过期』的说法。
错。Kafka 积压不是缓存过期瞬间的直接后果。
对。洪水打库，且每个请求都要等慢查询完成，SLA 破。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: these two terms aren't directly related to cache-expiry problems.
Wrong: a TTL cache is designed to lapse on a schedule, so 'never expires' doesn't apply.
Wrong: Kafka backlog isn't a direct consequence of cache expiry.
Correct: a flood hits the database, and every request waits on a slow recompute, breaking the SLA.
scenario: 纯 TTL 缓存挡住了绝大多数 Top-K 读，但一次窗口聚合仍要跑好几分钟。
scenario_en: A pure TTL cache absorbs almost all Top-K reads, but one window aggregation still takes several minutes.

q: 请求合并（coalescing）在缓存过期问题里能解决什么、解决不了什么？
q_en: What does request coalescing fix for cache expiry, and what does it not fix?
options: 洪水和 SLA 两个问题都能解决
两个问题都解决不了
能保护数据库，但救不了 SLA
只能解决 SLA，救不了数据库
why: 合并让同窗口只有一个请求真正打库，洪水没了；但所有等待者的延迟仍取决于那次慢查询，SLA 照样破，需要预计算来根治。
why_en: Request coalescing lets only one request per window hit the database and shields it, but everyone still waits on the slow recompute so the latency SLA is still broken.
options_en: It solves both the flood and the SLA problem.
It solves neither problem.
It protects the database, but it doesn't save the SLA.
It only fixes the SLA, not the database.
optionExplanations: 错。合并请求救不了 SLA，那次现算依旧超时。
错。它确实能挡住绝大部分打库请求，起到保护作用。
对。合并保护数据库，但等待者的延迟仍取决于那次慢查询。
错。合并解决的是数据库压力，不是 SLA 本身。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: coalescing doesn't save the SLA, that one live query still runs long.
Wrong: it does block most database-bound requests and offers real protection.
Correct: coalescing protects the database, but waiters' latency still depends on that slow query.
Wrong: coalescing addresses database load, not the SLA directly.
scenario: 缓存到期瞬间同一窗口涌来上万个并发 Top-K 请求，底层聚合仍需几分钟。
scenario_en: The moment the cache expires, tens of thousands of concurrent Top-K requests hit the same window while the underlying aggregation still takes minutes.

scenario: 缓存 TTL 到期瞬间总会破坏 SLA，希望读请求永远只读缓存、绝不触发现场查库。
scenario_en: Cache TTL expiry keeps breaking the SLA, so you want reads to always hit cache and never trigger an on-demand database query.
q: 该怎么改？
q_en: How should the cache-expiry problem be redesigned?
options: 把 TTL 设成无限长
加 cron 定时预计算并刷新缓存
加更多缓存副本
让客户端失败后重试三次
why: cron 以固定节奏跑在过期前面，读路径变成纯缓存读，窗口边界处的 SLA 问题根治；这正是「预计算」补上「缓存」短板的组合拳。
why_en: A cron job precomputes each window's top K on a fixed interval and warms the cache ahead of expiration, so reads never touch the database.
whenOtherWins: 如果读流量很小或新鲜度要求极宽松，简单 TTL 加请求合并就够了，不必引入 cron 的运维负担。
options_en: Set the TTL to infinite.
Add a cron job to precompute and proactively refresh the cache.
Add more cache replicas.
Have clients retry three times after a failure.
optionExplanations: 错。永不过期会让结果永远陈旧，不符合精确性要求。
对。cron 提前于过期时间跑，读路径彻底脱离数据库。
错。多副本能分摊读流量，但解决不了过期瞬间的洪水。
错。客户端重试只会在过期窗口内加重数据库压力。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: an infinite TTL leaves results permanently stale, breaking the precision requirement.
Correct: a cron job stays ahead of expiry, so reads always hit the cache and the SLA problem is solved.
Wrong: more replicas spread read traffic but don't fix the flood at the moment of expiry.
Wrong: client retries would only add more load to the database during the expiry window.
tradeoff: cron 预计算根治 SLA vs 纯 TTL 缓存简单但会击穿

q: 引入预计算 cron 的主要代价与兜底手段是？
q_en: What are the main cost and fallback for adding a precompute cron?
options: 代价是运维复杂度；兜底是多留几小时缓存
代价是读延迟上升；兜底是加索引
代价是数据永久丢失；兜底是备份
代价是缓存彻底失效；兜底是换数据库
why: cron 挂了、跑慢了都要监控和兜底，但这些运维细节不是本题重点，面试官一般不深挖；用「保留几小时 + 容忍短暂陈旧」兜住即可。
why_en: The cron approach adds operational complexity around failures and lag, mitigated by retaining cache entries for hours so stale data can be served instead of nothing.
options_en: Cost is operational complexity; the fallback is keeping cache entries longer.
Cost is higher read latency; the fallback is adding an index.
Cost is permanent data loss; the fallback is backups.
Cost is total cache failure; the fallback is switching databases.
optionExplanations: 对。运维复杂度是代价，多留缓存时长是兜底手段。
错。cron 不会让读延迟上升，读路径仍是纯缓存。
错。cron 失败不等于数据永久丢失。
错。cron 出问题不会让缓存整体失效。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: operational complexity is the cost, and keeping cache entries longer is the fallback.
Wrong: the cron doesn't raise read latency, reads still only hit the cache.
Wrong: a cron failure doesn't mean data is permanently lost.
Wrong: a cron issue doesn't take down the whole cache.
scenario: 改成 cron 定期预算窗口 Top-K 写进缓存，NFR 容忍结果最多旧 1 分钟。
scenario_en: We switch to a cron that periodically precomputes each window Top-K into the cache, and the NFR tolerates results up to a minute stale.

q: 把「扩展读路径」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the read-scaling decision chain in the correct order:
steps: 缓解：cron 定时预计算并提前刷缓存，读路径只碰缓存
需求：几十毫秒内返回，且允许结果落后最多 1 分钟
代价：TTL 过期瞬间请求洪水打库、SLA 被击穿
选型：Redis 缓存整个 Top-K 响应（键 = 窗口 + 截断时间戳）
why: 需求（快读 + 容忍 1 分钟旧）→ 缓存整个响应 → 过期洪水与 SLA 破 → cron 预计算跑在过期前面。这是本题读侧的主线决策。
why_en: The read-path chain runs from the latency requirement to caching the response, then the expiry flood problem, and finally cron precomputation that stays ahead of expirations.
diagram:
flowchart LR R["需求：几十毫秒返回
容忍 1 分钟延迟"] --> C["选型：缓存整个响应"] C --> K["代价：过期洪水 + SLA 破"] K --> M["缓解：cron 预计算刷缓存"]

q: 算出这个吞吐量级后，对数据库写入方案意味着什么？
q_en: Once you compute this throughput, what does it imply for database writes?
options: 写入量仍落在单机数据库可承受的范围内，完全不需要特殊处理
写入量远超单机数据库上限，写路径必须靠分片、批量聚合等扩展手段
只要给 views 列多加一个索引就能解决这个问题
这属于读扩展的问题，跟写路径设计完全没有关系
why: 70B views/day ÷ 10 万秒/天（简化心算）≈ 70 万 TPS，远超单机数据库量级，后面的分片与批量聚合都是为了扛住这个数字。
why_en: About seventy billion views a day divides out to roughly seven hundred thousand writes per second, far beyond a single database node, which is why sharding and batching come next.
scenario: 面试官给出 YouTube Shorts 日观看量约 700 亿次；你心算出对应的写入吞吐量级（用 10 万秒/天简化）。
scenario_en: The interviewer gives about seventy billion YouTube Shorts views per day, and you mentally convert it to write throughput using one hundred thousand seconds per day.
options_en: The write volume still sits within a single database node's capacity, no special handling needed at all.
The write volume far exceeds a single node's limit, so the write path must use sharding and batch aggregation.
Just adding one more index on the views column would settle this.
This is purely a read-scaling problem and has nothing to do with the write path.
optionExplanations: 错。约 70 万 TPS 比单机数据库的写入上限高出一两个数量级，靠不上『无需特殊处理』。
对。70 万级 TPS 只能靠分片承接压力、再用批量聚合压低写入条数来扛住。
错。索引只加快读取排序，改变不了每秒几十万次写入这个瓶颈。
错。这道题问的正是写入吞吐会不会压垮数据库，属于写路径设计。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: roughly 700k TPS is one to two orders of magnitude above what a single database can take, so 'no special handling' doesn't hold.
Correct: at ~700k TPS the write path has to lean on sharding plus batched aggregation to survive the load.
Wrong: an index speeds up sorted reads, it doesn't change a per-second write ceiling in the hundreds of thousands.
Wrong: this is precisely asking whether the database gets crushed on writes, so it's a write-path question.

q: 把两者一对比，对单库方案意味着什么？
q_en: Comparing those numbers, what does it imply for a single-database design?
options: 差距约 70 倍，单库方案不可行，必须做写扩展
差距其实很小，单库基本就能扛住压力
这个差距完全可以靠升级硬件抹平
差距只会影响读延迟，跟写入方案没有关系
why: 单节点 RDBMS 在合适条件下约 1 万+ 写/秒，对照本题约 70 万 TPS 的写入需求，差了约 70 倍，单库方案宣告出局。
why_en: A single relational database node tops out around ten thousand writes per second, roughly seventy times short of this system's estimated seven hundred thousand, which rules out a single-instance design.
scenario: 面试官提到现代关系型数据库单节点在合适条件下约能扛 1 万+ 次写/秒；对照本题约 70 万 TPS 的写入需求。
scenario_en: The interviewer says a modern relational database node can handle about ten thousand writes per second under good conditions, while this problem needs about seven hundred thousand TPS.
options_en: The gap is about seventy times, so a single database is not viable and write scaling is required.
The gap is actually small, a single database can basically hold up under the pressure.
This gap can be fully closed just by upgrading the hardware.
The gap only affects read latency and has nothing to do with the write plan.
optionExplanations: 对。1 万+ 对 70 万相差约两个数量级，单库写不动，必须靠分片等手段扩写。
错。两者相差约 70 倍，单库离『基本能扛住』还差得远。
错。升级硬件顶多带来常数倍提升，填不平近两个数量级的缺口。
错。这条差距直接决定写路径要不要分片，和读延迟无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: roughly 10k versus 700k is about a 70x gap, so a single database can't keep up and write scaling is required.
Wrong: the two are about 70x apart, far from 'basically manageable' for a single node.
Wrong: better hardware buys a constant-factor gain, not the near-two-orders-of-magnitude gap here.
Wrong: this gap decides whether the write path needs sharding, it has nothing to do with read latency.

q: 这个视频总量量级对后续设计意味着什么？
q_en: What does this video-count order of magnitude imply for later design?
options: videoId 基数达到十亿级，索引/聚合结构都要扛住
视频数量很小，可以整份放进单台服务器内存里随意遍历
只影响观看事件的字段格式，不影响存储设计
视频总量和写入吞吐没有任何关系
why: 1M 视频/天 × 365 × 10 年 ≈ 36 亿；凑整到 40 亿后，朴素 ID+计数表就要 64GB——这也是后面高基数问题（专用库选型）反复出现的根源。
why_en: About one million new videos a day over ten years adds up to roughly three point six billion videos, and that scale is why naive full counting tables and high-cardinality lookups keep showing up as a bottleneck later.
scenario: 按『每秒上传 1 小时内容、平均每个视频 6 分钟』估算，每天新增约 100 万条视频，十年后总视频数会到十亿级。
scenario_en: Using one hour of uploaded content per second and six minutes per average video, you estimate about one million new videos per day and billions over ten years.
options_en: VideoId cardinality reaches billions, so per-video structures must handle that scale.
The video count is small enough to fit entirely in one server's memory.
It only affects the field format of view events.
The total video count has nothing to do with write throughput.
optionExplanations: 对。videoId 基数冲到十亿级，索引和聚合结构从一开始就要按高基数设计。
错。十亿级实体远超单机内存能整份装下、随意遍历的规模。
错。基数这么大会直接影响存储与索引选型，不只是字段格式问题。
错。videoId 基数越大，后面维护的索引/聚合结构就越重，并非无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: videoId cardinality reaches the billions, so indexes and aggregation structures must be built for high cardinality from the start.
Wrong: a billion-scale entity set is far too large to hold entirely in one machine's memory for casual scans.
Wrong: this cardinality directly shapes storage and index choices, not just the view-event field format.
Wrong: a bigger videoId cardinality makes every index and aggregate structure heavier, so it is far from unrelated.

q: 补全存储估算：
q_en: Fill in the storage estimate:
text: 按 1M 视频/天 × 10 年，总视频数约 {{3.6B}} 个；凑成 4B 个后，朴素「ID + 计数」表 = 4B × (8 字节 ID + 8 字节计数) ≈ {{64}} GB——每保留一份全量视频计数集合都至少要这个量级。
why: 64 GB 是本题的关键锚点：任何「为每个窗口保存一份全量计数」的方案都要按这个量级乘上去，也解释了为什么全量哈希表放内存很贵。
why_en: About three point six billion videos at sixteen bytes each means every full set of per-video counts costs at least sixty-four gigabytes.
scenario: 你要把『新增视频数 × 十年』换算成存储代价的量级，判断朴素方案是否可行。
scenario_en: You need to convert new videos times ten years into a rough storage cost to decide whether the naive table shape is acceptable.

q: 关于面试中的估算，本文的核心建议是？
q_en: What is the article's core advice about estimation in interviews?
options: 所有题都必须先做完整的容量估算
数字必须精确到个位，体现严谨
需要且影响设计时才估算，重点是量级含义
估算永远可以跳过
why: 「estimate when you need it and when it might influence your design」；用 100k 秒/天这类凑整放心用，估算的产出是设计裁决而不是数字本身。
why_en: Estimate only when it influences the design, round aggressively, and focus on what the quantities imply about which architectures remain viable.
options_en: Every problem requires a complete capacity estimation up front.
Numbers must be precise to the last digit to show rigor.
Estimate only when needed, focusing on what the magnitude implies.
Estimation can always be skipped entirely.
optionExplanations: 错。不是每题都需要完整估算，看是否影响设计。
错。凑整反而是推荐做法，不追求算术精度。
对。只在需要且影响设计时估算，重点是量级带来的裁决。
错。当估算真的影响设计裁决时不能跳过。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: not every problem needs a full estimation, only when it matters.
Wrong: rounding is the recommended approach, not chasing arithmetic precision.
Correct: estimate only when needed, focusing on what the magnitude implies for the design.
Wrong: when an estimate actually influences the design, it shouldn't be skipped.
scenario: 45 分钟白板做 YouTube Shorts Top-K，估算最多值花两三分钟。
scenario_en: On a 45-minute whiteboard for Top-K on YouTube Shorts, estimation is worth two or three minutes at most.

scenario: 写入 700k TPS 而单库只能约 10k；上游 ViewEvent topic 已经按 video ID 分区。要用扩展写入的第一板斧扛住流量。
scenario_en: Writes are about seven hundred thousand TPS while one database can handle roughly ten thousand, and the upstream ViewEvent topic is already partitioned by video ID.
q: 怎么做？
q_en: How should we scale writes first?
options: 沿 videoId 键把消费者和数据库一起分片
换一台配置更大的单机数据库硬扛
把所有计数都塞进单个 Redis 实例里
干脆随机丢弃一半观看事件来减压
why: topic 已按 videoId 分区，这是天然的「缝」：沿同一键把消费者与数据库一起分片，每个分片持有一部分视频的完整计数。扩写入先想分片、分区、批量。
why_en: Scale out by sharding consumers and the database on the same video-ID key the topic is already partitioned by, so each shard holds a complete view of a subset of videos.
whenOtherWins: 若写入量在单库能力内（比如算单个 Spotify 用户的 top 歌单，单 CPU 就够），完全不需要分片。
options_en: Shard along the videoId key, sharding consumers and the database together.
Move to a bigger single-node database and push through on hardware alone.
Cram every counter into a single Redis instance.
Just randomly drop half the view events to relieve pressure.
optionExplanations: 对。沿已有分区键把消费者和数据库一起分片，是天然的缝。
错。再大的单机也很难追上 70 万 TPS 这个量级。
错。单个 Redis 实例同样会撞上单机写入上限。
错。丢事件破坏了『结果必须精确』这条硬性需求。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: sharding consumers and the database along the existing partition key is the natural seam.
Wrong: even a bigger single machine struggles to reach seven hundred thousand TPS.
Wrong: a single Redis instance still hits a single-node write ceiling.
Wrong: dropping events breaks the hard requirement that results be precise.
tradeoff: 沿现成分区键分片扩写 vs 单机纵向扩容

q: 算出所需分片数后，这对架构意味着什么？
q_en: After calculating the shard count, what does it imply for the architecture?
options: 分片数很少，一两个实例就够
分片数达到约 70 个，可行但明显浪费
分片数会超过一千，方案彻底不可行
分片数量和写入延迟无关，可以忽略
why: 700k ÷ 10k = 70 个分片；技术上可行，但为「计数」维护 70 个库明显过度，这正是引出批量聚合的动机。
why_en: Seven hundred thousand divided by ten thousand per shard is about seventy shards, technically workable but wasteful for something as simple as counting, which is exactly why batching comes next.
scenario: 把 700k TPS 的写入压到每个分片约 1 万 TPS 的水平。
scenario_en: You want to push seven hundred thousand TPS down to roughly ten thousand TPS per shard.
options_en: The shard count is tiny, one or two instances would be enough.
The shard count reaches about seventy, workable but clearly wasteful.
The shard count exceeds a thousand, making the plan infeasible.
Shard count has nothing to do with write latency.
optionExplanations: 错。700k 除以每分片 1 万这个量级，远不是一两台实例能兜住的。
对。70 个分片工程上跑得动，但为了存计数专门开 70 个库实例，代价明显不划算。
错。70 个分片数量不小，但还在可运维范围内，离上千个那种彻底失控还差得远。
错。分片数直接决定要运维多少库实例，这笔成本不能当作可以忽略的量。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: 700k divided by 10k per shard lands nowhere near 'one or two instances'.
Correct: about 70 shards can carry the load, but standing up 70 databases just to hold view counters is obvious overkill.
Wrong: 70 shards is a lot but still operable, nowhere close to the thousand-plus range that would sink the plan.
Wrong: shard count is exactly what decides how many database instances you run, it isn't something to wave away.

q: 分片后单条 SQL 拿不到全局 Top-K 了，如何保证结果仍然精确？
q_en: After sharding, how do we still produce an exact global Top-K?
options: 只查数据量最大的那个分片
查各分片自己的前 K 再归并
随机抽样几个分片近似
分片后全局 Top-K 无法再精确计算
why: 全局第 i 名在自己所属分片里的名次只会更靠前，所以取每个分片前 K 的并集必含全局前 K；top-K cron 改为对每个分片各查一次再归并。
why_en: Fetching the top K from every shard and merging is mathematically guaranteed to contain the global top K, since any global winner ranks at least that high on its own shard.
options_en: Only query the shard with the most data.
Query each shard for its own top K and merge them.
Randomly sample a few shards and approximate.
Once sharded, the global top K can no longer be computed precisely.
optionExplanations: 错。数据量最大的分片不一定包含全局排名靠前的视频。
对。全局第 i 名在自己分片内只会更靠前，并集必含全局前 K。
错。抽样违反了『结果必须精确』的硬性需求。
错。分片后依然能精确算出全局前 K，只是要多一步归并。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: the shard with the most data doesn't necessarily hold the globally top-ranked videos.
Correct: a global rank-i item ranks at least as high inside its own shard, so the union of per-shard top-Ks must contain the global top K.
Wrong: sampling violates the hard requirement that results be precise.
Wrong: the global top K can still be computed exactly after sharding, it just needs a merge step.
scenario: 700k TPS 写入逼得计数表按 videoId 分片，但需求仍要求 Top-K 结果精确。
scenario_en: Writes at 700k per second force us to shard the counter table by videoId, yet the requirement still demands an exact Top-K.

scenario: 70 个分片太浪费。你观察到任一时刻大量观看集中在少数爆款视频（Mr. Beast、Taylor Swift）上。
scenario_en: Seventy shards are wasteful, and at any moment a lot of views are concentrated on a small number of hit videos such as Mr. Beast or Taylor Swift.
q: 下一步优化是？
q_en: What is the next write-side optimization?
options: 把分片数量直接再翻一倍
把精确计数改成随机抽样估算
用 Flink 做流式预聚合，按小时攒批
整体换成一个 NoSQL 数据库
why: 观看高度集中于头部视频，把同一视频一小时内的多次观看合并成一条写即可大幅减写；Flink 自带批量、聚合与 checkpoint 恢复，还能处理事件迟到。
why_en: Use Flink to pre-aggregate views per video over an hour so many views collapse into one database write, exploiting the fact that most views hit a few popular videos.
whenOtherWins: 如果观看均匀散布在海量冷门视频上、聚合比很低，批量收益骤降，只能靠分片硬扛。
options_en: Simply double the shard count again.
Turn exact counting into a random-sampling estimate.
Use Flink to pre-aggregate the stream into hourly batches.
Switch the whole thing over to a NoSQL database.
optionExplanations: 错。再翻倍分片治标不治本，浪费只会加倍。
错。随机抽样违反『结果必须精确』的硬性需求。
对。同一视频一小时内多次观看合并成一条写，大幅减写。
错。换数据库类型解决不了写入次数过多的根本问题。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: doubling shards again treats the symptom and doubles the waste.
Wrong: random sampling violates the hard requirement that results be precise.
Correct: merging many views for the same video within an hour into one write cuts writes sharply.
Wrong: switching database type doesn't fix the root cause of too many writes.
tradeoff: 流式预聚合减写 vs 继续加分片硬扛

termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理框架，能做窗口聚合、批量攒批和状态容错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flink is a stream-processing framework that handles windowed aggregation, batching, and stateful fault tolerance.

q: 补全 Flink 批量聚合作业的两个关键配置：
q_en: Fill in the two key settings for the Flink batch aggregation job:
text: 用 BoundedOutOfOrderness 水位线策略最多等约 {{30 秒}}（留在 1 分钟预算内）接收迟到事件；用 {{1 小时}}的 tumbling 窗口聚合每个视频的观看数。
why: 水位线告诉 Flink 为迟到事件等多久（30 秒 < 1 分钟计入预算）；tumbling 小时窗口把逐条事件变成每视频每小时一条聚合输出。
why_en: The job waits up to thirty seconds for late events with a bounded-out-of-orderness watermark and aggregates views per video in one-hour tumbling windows.
diagram:
graph LR
    Views[View events] --> Kafka[Kafka]
    Kafka --> Flink[Flink batch window]
    Flink --> Agg[(Aggregate DB)]
    Agg --> Cache[(Top-K cache)]

q: Flink 节点挂掉时为什么不会丢观看数据？
q_en: Why does a Flink node failure not lose view data?
options: Flink 会把每条事件同步写三份
数据丢了就丢了，反正是近似
由 Postgres 负责补数据
从 checkpoint offset 重放
why: Flink 定期 checkpoint 状态和 Kafka 偏移；故障后从最近 checkpoint 恢复状态、从对应 offset 重放事件，不必担心丢数据或事件延迟这类棘手问题。
why_en: Flink checkpoints its state along with Kafka offsets, so after a failure it rewinds the topic to the last checkpoint and replays from there.
options_en: Flink synchronously writes every event to three copies.
Lost data is fine since this is an approximate system anyway.
Postgres is responsible for filling in the missing data.
Replay from the checkpoint offset.
optionExplanations: 错。Flink 靠 checkpoint 加重放，不是靠同步三写。
错。这一步方案仍要求精确，不能用『反正是近似』带过。
错。补数据不是 Postgres 的职责，这里还没引入 Postgres 依赖。
对。checkpoint 记住状态和 offset，故障后能从那里重放恢复。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: Flink relies on checkpointing and replay, not synchronous triple writes.
Wrong: this stage of the design still requires precision, not an approximate hand-wave.
Wrong: filling in missing data isn't Postgres's job, and there's no such dependency here.
Correct: checkpoints remember state and offset, so recovery replays from there after a failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: Flink 定期把作业状态和消费位点持久化的快照，用于故障恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A checkpoint is a periodic snapshot Flink takes of job state and consumer offsets, used to recover after a failure.

scenario: 视频观看聚合作业跑在 Flink 上，某个处理节点突然崩溃重启。
scenario_en: The video-view aggregation job runs in Flink, and one processing node suddenly crashes and restarts.

q: 批量化把写入模式变成了什么样？代价可接受吗？
q_en: What does batching turn the write pattern into, and is the tradeoff acceptable?
options: 变成每小时批量写，条数还能降 2-100 倍
写入节奏变得更均匀了，没什么变化
写入次数反而比之前增加了
数据必然会丢失，这是不可接受的代价
why: 批量把稳定流变成小时脉冲，但数据库天生擅长批量加载；聚合把同一视频的多次观看合成一条，条数降 2-100 倍。
why_en: Batching turns steady writes into hourly bulk loads that databases handle efficiently, and aggregation cuts write counts by anywhere from two to a hundred times.
options_en: It becomes an hourly batch write, and write count can drop by two to a hundred times.
The write rhythm becomes more even, nothing really changes.
The number of writes actually goes up compared to before.
Data loss becomes unavoidable, an unacceptable cost.
optionExplanations: 对。批量写只要分散到各分片就可接受，条数还能大降。
错。批量恰恰让写入从平稳流变成脉冲，不是更均匀。
错。聚合把多次观看合并成一条，写入次数是下降的。
错。批量聚合本身不会导致数据丢失，是独立的关注点。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: batching is fine as long as it spreads across shards, and write count can drop sharply.
Wrong: batching turns a steady stream into pulses, it isn't more even.
Wrong: aggregation merges multiple views into one write, so count goes down.
Wrong: batching itself doesn't cause data loss, that's a separate concern.
scenario: 消费者原本逐条写 Postgres，700k TPS 打爆单库；改成按小时聚合后批量写。
scenario_en: Consumers used to write one row per view into Postgres, which 700k writes per second flattens, so we aggregate per hour and write in batches.

q: 这对数据库分片规模意味着什么？
q_en: What does this mean for the database shard count?
options: 分片数能降到个位数到十位数量级，仍不完美但可管理
分片数完全不受影响，仍要维持约 70 个
只需要 1 个分片就够，无需再分片
分片数反而会继续增加
why: 聚合把写入条数压低一到两个数量级，70 个分片可以缩到 5-10 个的量级。
why_en: Aggregation cuts write volume by one to two orders of magnitude, so shard count drops from about seventy down to roughly five to ten.
scenario: 引入 Flink 批量聚合后，写入条数下降一到两个数量级。
scenario_en: After introducing Flink batch aggregation, the number of database writes drops by one to two orders of magnitude.
options_en: Shard count can drop to single or low double digits, still imperfect but manageable.
Shard count is unaffected and still needs about seventy.
Just one shard is enough, no more sharding needed.
Shard count actually keeps increasing.
optionExplanations: 对。写入压力大幅降下来后，分片规模能收进个位数到十几的区间，虽不完美但可管理。
错。写入量都降了这么多，还死守 70 个分片就是明显的资源浪费。
错。聚合只是把写入条数往下压，还没压到单个分片就能兜住的地步。
错。聚合正是让写入条数往下走的动作，分片需求只会跟着往下降，不会增加。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: with far fewer writes to handle, the shard count settles into single digits or the low teens, workable if not perfectly clean.
Wrong: keeping all seventy shards once writes have dropped this much is simply over-provisioned.
Wrong: batching only trims write volume, it doesn't shrink demand down to what a lone shard can absorb.
Wrong: aggregation is precisely what pulls write volume down, so shard count should follow it lower, not rise.

q: 把「扛住写入」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the write-scaling decision chain in the correct order:
steps: 优化：Flink 按视频批量聚合（1 小时 tumbling 窗口），写库条数降 2-100 倍，分片缩到 5-10 个
选型：沿 Kafka 的 videoId 分区键，把消费者和数据库一起分片
需求：70B views/day ≈ 800k TPS，远超单库约 10k 的能力
代价：压到每片 10k TPS 需要 70 个库，对简单计数太浪费
why: 估算暴露约 800k TPS（70B/day / 86,400s）→ 沿分区键分片 → 直接按峰值拆库太浪费 → 批量聚合把写入压到个位数分片。写侧两板斧：先分片，再批量。
why_en: The write-path chain goes from the roughly eight-hundred-thousand writes-per-second estimate to sharding on the video-ID key, then the shard cost, and finally Flink batching that shrinks writes to a handful.
diagram:
graph TD
    Raw[~800k events per sec] --> Shard[Shard writes]
    Shard --> TooMany[Too many DB writes]
    TooMany --> Batch[Flink aggregation]
    Batch --> Fewer[Fewer aggregate upserts]

q: 缓存未命中或预计算时执行的窗口 Top-K 查询，为什么耗时以「分钟到小时」计？
q_en: Why can a cache-miss or precompute window Top-K query take minutes to hours?
options: 网络往返太慢
SQL 引擎实现有缺陷
缓存容量不够
要先聚合数百 GB 再取前 K
why: 两步操作（窗口内逐行求和 + 聚合后取前 K）绕不开对数百 GB 数据的处理；数据量直接决定时间量级。
why_en: The query must sum every row in the window before extracting the top K, and crunching hundreds of gigabytes takes minutes or hours rather than seconds.
options_en: The network round trip is too slow.
The SQL engine implementation is flawed.
The cache doesn't have enough capacity.
It must aggregate hundreds of gigabytes before taking the top K.
optionExplanations: 错。慢的根源是数据量，不是网络往返。
错。SQL 引擎本身没有缺陷，是查询形态太重。
错。这条查询不是从缓存读的，缓存容量不是原因。
对。要先聚合窗口内全量数据、再取前 K，数据量决定耗时。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: the slowness comes from data volume, not the network round trip.
Wrong: the SQL engine itself isn't flawed, the query shape is just heavy.
Wrong: this query isn't served from cache, so cache capacity isn't the cause.
Correct: it must aggregate the full window before taking the top K, and data volume dictates the time.
scenario: 一个小时窗口的明细有数百 GB，缓存未命中时要现场聚合再取前 K。
scenario_en: One hour window holds hundreds of gigabytes of raw rows, and on a cache miss we must aggregate them and then take the top K.

q: 把窗口聚合搬到 Spark/Hadoop 上的局限是？
q_en: What is the limitation of moving window aggregation to Spark or Hadoop?
options: Spark 不支持聚合运算
Hadoop 无法读取数据库
并行化能加速但要付出更多容量成本
完全没有任何收益
why: 并行计算平台同样受总计算量约束，加速靠加机器换来；高分答案是改变数据组织方式让问题本身变小。
why_en: Spark parallelizes the scan but pays in capacity and cost, and senior interviewers want you to simplify the problem rather than throw hardware at it.
options_en: Spark doesn't support aggregation operations.
Hadoop cannot read from a database.
Parallelization speeds things up but costs more capacity.
There is no benefit at all.
optionExplanations: 错。Spark 完全支持聚合运算，这不是它的限制。
错。Hadoop 能够读取数据库数据，这不是限制所在。
对。并行计算能加速但要付出容量成本，高分答案是简化问题。
错。并行化确实带来加速收益，不能说完全没有。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: Spark fully supports aggregation, that's not its limitation.
Wrong: Hadoop can read database data, that's not the limitation here.
Correct: parallelization speeds things up but costs more capacity; a strong answer simplifies the problem instead.
Wrong: parallelization does bring real speedup, so 'no benefit' is inaccurate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式批处理计算框架，常用于大规模数据聚合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Spark is a distributed batch-processing framework commonly used for large-scale data aggregation.

scenario: 窗口聚合要处理数百 GB，团队想直接扔给 Spark/Hadoop 集群并行跑。
scenario_en: The window aggregation touches hundreds of gigabytes, and the team wants to just hand it to a Spark or Hadoop cluster to parallelize.

scenario: 月窗口查询要对每个视频聚合 24 × 30 = 720 条小时粒度记录，太慢。想减少大窗口查询要处理的记录数。
scenario_en: A monthly window query has to aggregate 24 times 30 hourly rows per video, which is too slow, so you want to reduce the records scanned for large windows.
q: 第一个改进思路是？
q_en: What is the first improvement for large window queries?
options: 删掉月窗口这个功能
多维护一层天级聚合
给查询加更多内存
把索引改成哈希索引
why: 月查询从每视频扫 720 条降到约 30 条；粗粒度既可用 cron 从细粒度汇总，也可让 Flink 同时维护多个窗口状态直接输出到新表。
why_en: Maintain coarser day-level aggregates alongside hourly ones so month queries sum about thirty daily rows per video instead of seven hundred twenty hourly ones.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需支持小时级窗口，单一小时粒度就够了，不必引入多粒度表的复杂度。
options_en: Remove the monthly window feature entirely.
Maintain a coarser daily rollup alongside the hourly one.
Just add more memory to the query.
Switch the index to a hash index.
optionExplanations: 错。砍掉功能不是优化，是放弃需求。
对。加一层天级聚合，月查询记录数从 720 降到约 30。
错。加内存解决不了要读的记录数量本身。
错。哈希索引不支持范围/排序查询，帮不上这里的忙。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: removing the feature isn't optimization, it's giving up the requirement.
Correct: adding a daily rollup drops the record count a monthly query reads from 720 to about 30.
Wrong: more memory doesn't reduce the number of records that must be read.
Wrong: a hash index doesn't support range or ordered queries, so it doesn't help here.
tradeoff: 多维护一层粗粒度聚合 vs 现场汇总更细粒度记录

q: 「cron 从细粒度汇总出粗粒度」这个方案的痛点是？
q_en: What is painful about the cron that rolls fine-grained data into coarser summaries?
options: 天级聚合数学上不正确
无法支持月窗口
cron 读写加重库负载，链路也长
Flink 不支持同时维护多个窗口
why: 延迟链条长且库压力更大；可以辩护说大窗口榜单变化慢、用户新鲜度期望低，但每窗口聚合表是更好的方案。
why_en: The cron adds load to a strained database and worst-case freshness waits on the whole write-cron-aggregate-write-read chain, defensible only because long windows change slowly.
options_en: Daily aggregation is mathematically incorrect.
It cannot support the monthly window at all.
The cron's reads and writes add load, and the chain is long.
Flink cannot maintain multiple windows at once.
optionExplanations: 错。天级聚合在数学上完全正确，问题不在正确性。
错。这个方案确实能支持月窗口，只是链路长、慢。
对。cron 读写加重数据库负担，最坏情形延迟链条很长。
错。Flink 能同时维护多个窗口，这不是限制点。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: daily aggregation is mathematically correct, that's not the issue.
Wrong: this approach can support the monthly window, it's just slow and roundabout.
Correct: the cron's read/write load strains the database, and worst case the delay chain is long.
Wrong: Flink can maintain multiple windows at once, that's not the limitation.
scenario: 分钟级明细已落库，用 cron 逐级汇总出时/天/月榜单，而库已被 700k TPS 压着。
scenario_en: Minute-level rows already land in the database, and a cron rolls them up into hour, day, and month leaderboards while the database is already carrying 700k writes per second.

scenario: 希望 top-K cron 的查询回到「直接读索引、近似 O(k)」的形态，完全不做现场求和。
scenario_en: You want the Top-K cron query to become an index read that is nearly O(k), with no on-the-fly summing.
q: 数据应该怎么组织？
q_en: How should the data be organized for fast Top-K reads?
options: 所有数据存一张大宽表
每窗口一张带索引的聚合表
查询时动态创建临时表
把全部计数搬进应用内存
why: 每窗口一张预聚合表加 views 索引，读回到 O(k)；cron 只需从索引头部读前 K。这是「为查询形态组织数据」的典型操作。
why_en: Keep one continuously updated aggregate table per window with an index on views so the top-K cron reads results straight off a sorted index.
whenOtherWins: 若要支持任意时间段查询，固定窗口聚合表就失效了，只能退回通用时间序列存储加现场聚合。
options_en: Store everything in one giant wide table.
Maintain one indexed aggregate table per window.
Create a temporary table dynamically at query time.
Move all counts into application memory.
optionExplanations: 错。一张大宽表无法给每个窗口都提供有序索引读取。
对。每窗口一张带索引的聚合表，cron 直接读索引头部。
错。查询时建临时表远比预先维护索引慢。
错。全量计数放进应用内存既不持久也难以扩容。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: one giant wide table can't give every window its own indexed, sorted read.
Correct: one indexed aggregate table per window lets the cron read straight off the index head.
Wrong: creating a temp table at query time is far slower than a pre-maintained index.
Wrong: holding all counts in application memory isn't durable or easy to scale.
tradeoff: 每窗口一张预聚合索引表 vs 现场对细粒度记录求和

q: 「每窗口一张聚合表」方案把复杂度移到了哪里？
q_en: Where does the per-window aggregate-table design move the complexity?
options: 从读侧移到写侧
移到了客户端
移到了 Kafka
复杂度凭空消失了
why: 读变 O(k) 的代价是写放大：hour/day/month/all-time 四张表都要更新。系统设计的常态——复杂度不消失，只转移。

options_en: From reads to writes.
It moves to the client.
It moves to Kafka.
The complexity simply disappears.
optionExplanations: 对。读变快的代价是写放大：四张窗口表都要更新。
错。客户端不参与聚合表的写入逻辑。

Wrong: the client has no role in writing the aggregate tables.

q: 为 Postgres 批量写入做经验性调优时，可用的手段有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which empirical Postgres batch-write tuning options can help?
options: 用 unlogged table 避免写 WAL
把 fsync 推迟到事务结束
选好批大小（batch size），依赖基准测试验证
删除主键约束
why: 这些都是「经验性」优化，效果依赖具体数据和硬件，多半超出系统设计面试范围——点到为止并强调 benchmark 即可。
why_en: You can use unlogged tables to skip the write-ahead log, delay fsync to the end of the transaction, and tune batch sizes with benchmarks.
options_en: Use unlogged tables to skip writing to the WAL.
Delay fsync until the transaction ends.
Pick a good batch size, validated by benchmarking.
Drop the primary key constraint.

对。推迟 fsync 到事务结束能减少同步落盘次数。
对。批大小要靠基准测试验证，没有放之四海的固定值。
错。删主键约束丢失去重能力，不是标准优化手段。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: unlogged tables skip WAL writes, speeding up bulk inserts.
Correct: delaying fsync to transaction end reduces sync-to-disk calls.
Correct: batch size should be benchmarked, there's no universal fixed value.
Wrong: dropping the primary key loses deduplication and isn't a standard optimization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预写日志，数据库先写日志再改数据以保证崩溃后可恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The write-ahead log records changes before they're applied, so the database can recover after a crash.

termDefinitions.meaning: 强制把缓冲区数据刷到磁盘的系统调用。

scenario: 消费者每小时向 Postgres 批量灌入聚合行，写吞吐是当前瓶颈。
scenario_en: Consumers bulk-load aggregated rows into Postgres every hour, and write throughput is the current bottleneck.

scenario: 想更进一步简化架构：干掉 Postgres，让整条管道只剩流处理和缓存。
scenario_en: You want to simplify further by removing Postgres so the pipeline only has stream processing and cache.
q: 怎么做？
q_en: How can we simplify the architecture further by removing Postgres?
options: 干脆用更多 Postgres 分片来硬扛压力
让客户端自己在本地聚合观看数据
把原始事件永久留在 Kafka 里，按需回放读取
状态留在 Flink 里，用 RocksDB 扩容，直写缓存
why: Flink 原生分布式状态管理加 RocksDB 外部状态后端可承载大状态；Top-K 在作业内算好、分钟级直写缓存，Postgres 和 top-K cron 全部省掉。
why_en: Keep window aggregates in Flink state backed by RocksDB, compute the top K inside the job, and sink results straight to the cache every minute, eliminating Postgres entirely.
whenOtherWins: 面试官不熟 Flink、或明确要求「不用 Flink 做」时，Postgres 窗口聚合表方案更稳，不会滑向编码面试。
options_en: Just throw more Postgres shards at the pressure and push through.
Have clients aggregate their own view counts locally.
Keep raw events in Kafka forever and replay them on demand when needed.
Keep state in Flink with RocksDB, and write straight into the cache.
optionExplanations: 错。加更多分片没有减少组件，反而更复杂。
错。客户端聚合既不可信也无法保证一致性。
错。永久回放原始事件延迟太高，无法满足读 SLA。
对。状态留在 Flink，用 RocksDB 扩容，直写缓存去掉 Postgres。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: adding more shards doesn't remove a component, it adds more complexity.
Wrong: client-side aggregation is untrustworthy and can't guarantee consistency.
Wrong: permanently replaying raw events is too slow for the read SLA.
Correct: keep state in Flink, scale with RocksDB, and write straight to cache, dropping Postgres.

termDefinitions.meaning: 嵌入式键值存储，Flink 常用它把状态存到磁盘以支持超大状态。

q: 纯 Flink 方案的作业结构是？
q_en: What is the job structure of the pure Flink design?
options: 单个 map 算子完成所有工作
两个独立 Kafka topic 互相转发
Flink 定期查询 Postgres 再写缓存
按视频 keyBy 聚合窗口计数，再按窗口用堆维护前 K
why: 两级 keyed process function：先按视频聚每窗口计数，再按窗口用堆维护前 K，最后由 sink 写入 Redis sorted set。
why_en: The job keys events by video for rolling window counts, then keys the counts by window for a heap-based top-K aggregator, and finally sinks results to Redis.
diagram:
flowchart LR K["Kafka 观看事件"] --> A["keyBy videoId
滚动窗口聚合"] A --> B["keyBy window
TopK 聚合（堆）"] B --> R["Redis sink"]
options_en: A single map operator does all the work.
Two independent Kafka topics forward to each other.
Flink periodically queries Postgres and then writes to the cache.
Keyed per-video window aggregation feeds a per-window top-K heap.
optionExplanations: 错。单个 map 算子做不了窗口聚合和排名维护。
错。两个 topic 互转和这个作业结构无关。
错。这套方案已经不再依赖 Postgres 查询。
对。两级 keyBy：先按视频聚合窗口计数，再按窗口维护堆。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: a single map operator can't handle windowed aggregation and rank maintenance.
Wrong: two topics forwarding to each other has nothing to do with this job structure.
Wrong: this approach no longer depends on querying Postgres.
Correct: two keyed stages, first per-video window sums, then a per-window heap for top-K.

termDefinitions.meaning: 维护『前 K 大』的经典数据结构，插入/替换是对数级操作。

termDefinitions.meaning: Flink 里按某个字段把流分区，使同一 key 的事件进同一实例处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: keyBy partitions a Flink stream by a field so all events for the same key are processed by the same instance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式消息流平台，Flink 作业从这里读取观看事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed streaming platform that this Flink job reads view events from.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理框架，这里承载全部聚合与 Top-K 计算状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flink is a stream-processing framework holding all the aggregation and top-K state here.

scenario: 决定把 Postgres 全部去掉，只用 Flink 状态和缓存完成聚合与 Top-K 计算。
scenario_en: Postgres has been removed, and Flink state plus cache now handle aggregation and Top-K computation.

q: 纯 Flink 方案在面试里的最大风险是？
q_en: What is the biggest interview risk of the pure Flink design?
options: 严重依赖双方都懂 Flink
吞吐性能不够
无法容错恢复
云上部署成本过高
why: 方案优雅但吃前置知识，被追问底层时会偏离高层系统设计；文章态度是「为完整性介绍，一般不推荐」。
why_en: The all-Flink design depends on both sides knowing Flink well, and pushback can turn the session into a coding exercise, so it is generally not recommended for interviews.
options_en: It heavily depends on both sides knowing Flink.
Throughput isn't good enough.
It cannot recover from failures.
Cloud deployment cost is too high.
optionExplanations: 对。方案吃前置知识，容易被要求降级或深挖细节，文章整体不推荐。
错。纯 Flink 方案的吞吐其实是三个方案里最高的。
错。checkpoint 加 Kafka 重放能提供良好的容错恢复。
错。云成本不是文章提到的主要风险点。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: it demands shared Flink knowledge, invites deeper probing, and the article generally advises against it.
Wrong: throughput is actually the best of the three approaches here.

Wrong: cloud cost isn't the main risk the article calls out.

scenario_en: In a system design interview, you propose a design based entirely on Flink state management with no Postgres persistence layer.

q: 用数据库聚合表支持 sliding window 的核心维护机制是？
q_en: What is the core maintenance mechanism for sliding windows using aggregate tables?
options: 每分钟把整个窗口重新算一遍
新一分钟做增量，滑出的一分钟做减量
只加不减，靠 TTL 自动清理
用数据库触发器自动维护
why: 滑动窗口的本质是增量进、减量出：新一分钟 +，滑出的那一分钟 −；每个窗口（时/天/月）都这么维护。
why_en: A sliding aggregate is maintained by adding the newest minute of views and subtracting the minute that just slid out of the window.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    N["最近 1 分钟的观看"] -->|+ 增量| W["VideoViewsLastHour"]
    O["T-60 分钟那一分钟的观看"] -->|- 减量| W
options_en: Recompute the entire window from scratch every minute.
The newest minute is added and the minute that slid out is subtracted.
Only add, never subtract, and let TTL clean up automatically.
Use a database trigger to maintain it automatically.
optionExplanations: 错。整窗口重算代价巨大，违背了增量维护的初衷。
对。新一分钟做加法，滑出的那一分钟做减法。
错。只加不减无法反映『滑出窗口』这个语义。
错。文章方案靠 Flink/应用逻辑维护，不是数据库触发器。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: recomputing the whole window is prohibitively expensive and defeats incremental maintenance.
Correct: the newest minute is added and the minute that slid out is subtracted.
Wrong: add-only with TTL cleanup can't express the 'slid out of window' semantics.
Wrong: this design maintains it via Flink and application logic, not a database trigger.
scenario: 需求从 tumbling 改成 sliding：10:06 查「最近 1 小时」必须返回 9:06–10:06 的结果。
scenario_en: The requirement shifts from tumbling to sliding, so a query at 10:06 for the last hour must cover 9:06 to 10:06.

q: sliding 版「最近一小时」的每分钟落库流程是？
q_en: What is the per-minute persistence flow for the sliding one-hour window?
options: 直接覆盖整张窗口表
每小时全量重建一次
分钟聚合后读减量、写增量、按差值更新
只写增量，减量交给数据库清理任务
why: 分钟粒度聚合后走「读减量、写增量、按差值更新窗口表」三步；对 hour/day/month 每个窗口都执行这一套。
why_en: Each minute Flink emits minute-grain sums, the pipeline reads the minute falling out of the window as the decrement, writes the new minute, and updates the window table with the difference.

graph LR
    New[New minute bucket] --> Add[Add counts to 1h window]
    Old[Minute leaving window] --> Sub[Subtract counts]
    Add --> TopK[Update Top-K]
    Sub --> TopK
options_en: Overwrite the entire window table directly.
Fully rebuild the table once per hour.
Aggregate per minute, then read the decrement, write the increment, update by the difference.
Only write the increment; let a cleanup job handle the decrement.
optionExplanations: 错。直接覆盖整表丢失了增量维护的意义。
错。全量重建代价太大，违背滑动窗口的设计初衷。
对。分钟级聚合后读减量、写增量、按差值更新窗口表。
错。减量必须和增量同步处理，不能交给独立清理任务。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: overwriting the whole table defeats the point of incremental maintenance.
Wrong: a full hourly rebuild is too costly and defeats the sliding-window design.
Correct: aggregate per minute, read the decrement, write the increment, update by the net difference.
Wrong: the decrement must be handled alongside the increment, not by a separate cleanup job.

scenario_en: A sliding last-hour window has to move continuously with the clock, and raw events are aggregated per minute before landing.

q: 补全滑动窗口的维护公式：
q_en: Fill in the sliding-window maintenance formula:
text: 滑动窗口维护：新一分钟的观看做{{增量}}，滑出窗口的那一分钟的观看做{{减量}}；all-time 窗口的减量恒为 {{0}}。
why: 增减对称是滑动窗口的记忆锚点；all-time 永不滑出所以只加不减，这也是它最容易维护的原因。
why_en: Sliding windows add the newest minute and subtract the expiring minute, while the all-time window never subtracts anything.

q: sliding window 方案给数据库带来的两大额外负担是？
q_en: What two extra burdens does the sliding-window design put on the database?
options: 只是磁盘略贵一点
变成读改写，还要留一月明细
索引会失效
Kafka 消费速度跟不上

options_en: It's only a bit more expensive on disk.
It becomes read-modify-write, and a month of detail must be retained.
Indexes stop working.
Kafka consumption can't keep up.

对。读改写比 append 重得多，还要多留一个月明细数据。
错。索引本身仍然有效，问题不是索引失效。
错。Kafka 消费速度不是这个方案带来的直接问题。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: disk cost is a small part of the problem, not the main burden.
